{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN5LKRC21vAQ4jHXTE9d","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SXvoYtqoHc7NMdhVVyApMj","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Quakes/runs/20261025.010423/build/Quakes/cli/options.py","content":"\"\"\"Parse and validate the command line into a `Parsed` record.\n\nParsing never touches the file system and never prints. Every malformed invocation raises\n`UsageError`, which `main` maps to exit code 2. The grammar is hand-written rather than argparse so\nthat numeric values, repeated options, and extra positionals follow FEATURE-Options exactly.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\n\nDEFAULT_TOP_COUNT = 10\nDEFAULT_FETCH_MIN_MAG = 2.5\n\n_NUMBER = re.compile(r\"-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n_COUNT = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+\")\n_DATE = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Parsed:\n    \"\"\"A validated invocation. Options a command does not take keep their defaults.\"\"\"\n\n    command: str\n    min_mag: float | None = None\n    n: int = DEFAULT_TOP_COUNT\n    lat: float | None = None\n    lon: float | None = None\n    radius: float | None = None\n    start: str | None = None\n    end: str | None = None\n    out: str | None = None\n    file: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _Spec:\n    \"\"\"Which options a command takes, which it requires, and whether it takes the file argument.\"\"\"\n\n    options: frozenset[str]\n    required: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n    takes_file: bool = True\n\n\n_MIN_MAG = \"--min-mag\"\n\n_SPECS: dict[str, _Spec] = {\n    \"fetch\": _Spec(\n        options=frozenset({\"--start\", \"--end\", \"--min-mag\", \"--out\"}),\n        required=frozenset({\"--start\", \"--end\", \"--out\"}),\n        takes_file=False,\n    ),\n    \"summary\": _Spec(options=frozenset({_MIN_MAG})),\n    \"top\": _Spec(options=frozenset({_MIN_MAG, \"--n\"})),\n    \"daily\": _Spec(options=frozenset({_MIN_MAG})),\n    \"regions\": _Spec(options=frozenset({_MIN_MAG})),\n    \"near\": _Spec(\n        options=frozenset({\"--lat\", \"--lon\", \"--radius\", _MIN_MAG}),\n        required=frozenset({\"--lat\", \"--lon\", \"--radius\"}),\n    ),\n}\n\n\ndef parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Parsed:\n    \"\"\"Return the validated `Parsed` for `argv`, or raise `UsageError` for any malformed invocation.\"\"\"\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"missing command\")\n    command, rest = argv[0], argv[1:]\n    spec = _SPECS.get(command)\n    if spec is None:\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {command!r}\")\n\n    raw = _collect_options(command, spec, rest)\n    positionals = _collect_positionals(rest, spec)\n    missing = sorted(spec.required - raw.keys())\n    if missing:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n    if spec.takes_file and len(positionals) != 1:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} requires exactly one file argument\")\n    if not spec.takes_file and positionals:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} takes no file argument: {positionals[0]!r}\")\n\n    min_mag_default = DEFAULT_FETCH_MIN_MAG if command == \"fetch\" else None\n    return Parsed(\n        command=command,\n        min_mag=_number(raw[_MIN_MAG], _MIN_MAG) if _MIN_MAG in raw else min_mag_default,\n        n=_count(raw[\"--n\"]) if \"--n\" in raw else DEFAULT_TOP_COUNT,\n        lat=_ranged(raw, \"--lat\", -90.0, 90.0),\n        lon=_ranged(raw, \"--lon\", -180.0, 180.0),\n        radius=_positive(raw, \"--radius\"),\n        start=_date(raw[\"--start\"], \"--start\") if \"--start\" in raw else None,\n        end=_date(raw[\"--end\"], \"--end\") if \"--end\" in raw else None,\n        out=_non_empty(raw[\"--out\"], \"--out\") if \"--out\" in raw else None,\n        file=positionals[0] if positionals else None,\n    )\n\n\ndef _collect_options(command: str, spec: _Spec, rest: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Map each option the command takes to its raw value; reject unknown, repeated, or valueless ones.\"\"\"\n    raw: dict[str, str] = {}\n    i = 0\n    while i < len(rest):\n        token = rest[i]\n        if not token.startswith(\"--\"):\n            i += 1\n            continue\n        if token not in spec.options:\n            raise UsageError(f\"{command} does not accept {token}\")\n        if token in raw:\n            raise UsageError(f\"{token} given more than once\")\n        if i + 1 >= len(rest) or rest[i + 1] in spec.options:\n            raise UsageError(f\"{token} requires a value\")\n        raw[token] = rest[i + 1]\n        i += 2\n    return raw\n\n\ndef _collect_positionals(rest: list[str], spec: _Spec) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return the non-option tokens, skipping each option's value; a stray dash-token is malformed.\"\"\"\n    positionals: list[str] = []\n    i = 0\n    while i < len(rest):\n        token = rest[i]\n        if token.startswith(\"--\"):\n            i += 2\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\") and token != \"-\":\n            raise UsageError(f\"unknown option: {token!r}\")\n        positionals.append(token)\n        i += 1\n    return positionals\n\n\ndef _number(text: str, option: str) -> float:\n    if not _NUMBER.fullmatch(text):\n        raise UsageError(f\"{option} expects a decimal number, got {text!r}\")\n    return float(text)\n\n\ndef _count(text: str) -> int:\n    if not _COUNT.fullmatch(text) or int(text) == 0:\n        raise UsageError(f\"--n expects a positive integer, got {text!r}\")\n    return int(text)\n\n\ndef _ranged(raw: dict[str, str], option: str, low: float, high: float) -> float | None:\n    if option not in raw:\n        return None\n    value = _number(raw[option], option)\n    if not low <= value <= high:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{option} must be within {low:g} to {high:g}, got {raw[option]!r}\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _positive(raw: dict[str, str], option: str) -> float | None:\n    if option not in raw:\n        return None\n    value = _number(raw[option], option)\n    if value <= 0:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{option} must be greater than zero, got {raw[option]!r}\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _date(text: str, option: str) -> str:\n    if not _DATE.fullmatch(text):\n        raise UsageError(f\"{option} expects YYYY-MM-DD, got {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as UsageError(f\"{option} must not be empty\")\n    return \"\"\"Which options a command takes, which it requires, and whether it takes the file argument.\"\"\"\n\n    options: frozenset[str]\n    required: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n    takes_file: bool = ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal\nfrom typing import Any, TextIO\n\n_EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n_ISO_UTC = \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"\n_ONE_PLACE = Decimal(\"0.1\")\n_TWO_PLACES = Decimal(\"0.01\")\n\n\ndef format_time(ms: int | float) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return epoch milliseconds as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, truncated to whole seconds.\"\"\"\n    seconds = math.floor(ms) // format_decimal(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a depth or distance with one decimal place, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _ONE_PLACE)\n\n\ndef render_csv(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as CSV text with `\\\\n` line endings; fields with commas or quotes are quoted.\"\"\"\n    buffer = io.StringIO()\n    csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator=\"\\n\").writerows(rows)\n    return buffer.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write_csv(rows: list[list[str]], stream: TextIO | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write `render_csv(rows)` to `stream`, or to standard output as UTF-8 when `stream` is None.\"\"\"\n    text = render_csv(rows)\n    if stream is not None:\n        stream.write(text)\n        return\n    out = sys.stdout\n    binary = getattr(out, \"buffer\", None)\n    if binary is not None:\n        out.flush()\n        binary.write(text.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        binary.flush()\n    else:\n        out.write(text)\n\n\ndef formatting for every report: UTC times, rounded numbers, and CSV text.\n\nRounding goes through `Decimal(repr(x))` with `ROUND_HALF_UP` (decision Q-002), never through the\nbuilt-in `round()`, so exact halves such as 0.25 and 5.125 round up on every platform.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport math\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone\nfrom decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal\nfrom typing import Any, TextIO\n\n_EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n_ISO_UTC = \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"\n_ONE_PLACE = Decimal(\"0.1\")\n_TWO_PLACES = Decimal(\"0.01\")\n\n\ndef format_time(ms: int | float) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return epoch milliseconds as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, truncated to whole seconds.\"\"\"\n    seconds = math.floor(ms) // 1000\n    return (_EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=seconds)).strftime(_ISO_UTC)\n\n\ndef format_mag(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a magnitude with exactly one decimal place, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _ONE_PLACE)\n\n\ndef format_mean(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a mean magnitude with two decimal places, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _TWO_PLACES)\n\n\ndef format_decimal(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a depth or distance with one decimal place, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _ONE_PLACE)\n\n\ndef render_csv(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as CSV text with `\\\\n` line endings; fields with commas or quotes are quoted.\"\"\"\n    buffer = io.StringIO()\n    csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator=\"\\n\").writerows(rows)\n    return buffer.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write_csv(rows: list[list[str]], stream: TextIO | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write `render_csv(rows)` to `stream`, or to standard output as UTF-8 when `stream` is None.\"\"\"\n    text = render_csv(rows)\n    if stream is not None:\n        stream.write(text)\n        return\n    out = sys.stdout\n    binary = getattr(out, \"buffer\", None)\n    if binary is not None:\n        out.flush()\n        binary.write(text.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        binary.flush()\n    else:\n        out.write(text)\n\n\ndef _quantize(x: Any, places: Decimal) -> str:\n    return str(Decimal(repr(x)).quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01CgnVtKQMcCyvcTcUqoFTfn","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN5Mb82vuqmJ2izGq7zm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EUTrSEfH8xCZusaGztCN6i","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Quakes/runs/20261025.010423/build/Quakes/cli/feed.py","content":"\"\"\"Read a saved USGS GeoJSON feed, extract event records, and apply the magnitude filter.\n\nEach function here is pure apart from `read_feed`, which reads one file. Failures surface only as\n`OperationalError`; nothing is written to standard output.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Event:\n    \"\"\"One earthquake, reduced to the fields the reports need.\"\"\"\n\n    id: str\n    mag: float\n    place: str | None\n    time_ms: int\n    tsunami: int\n    lon: float\n    lat: float\n    depth_km: float\n\n\ndef read_feed(path: str | Path) -> list[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return the `features` array of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection file, unchanged.\n\n    Raises `OperationalError` when the file cannot be read, is not JSON, or is not a FeatureCollection\n    object whose `features` value is an array.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}\") from exc\n    try:\n        document = json.loads(text)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not valid JSON\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get(\"type\") != \"FeatureCollection\":\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not a GeoJSON FeatureCollection\")\n    features = document.get(\"features\")\n    if not isinstance(features, list):\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} has no features array\")\n    return features\n\n\ndef extract_events(features: list[Any]) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Turn feed features into `Event` records in feed order, dropping events whose magnitude is null.\"\"\"\n    return [event for event in (_event(feature) for feature in features) if event is not None]\n\n\ndef filter_events(events: list[Event], min_mag: float | None) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Keep events with `mag >= min_mag`, in order. `None` keeps every event.\"\"\"\n    if min_mag is None:\n        return list(events)\n    return [event for event in events if event.mag >= min_mag]\n\n\ndef _event(feature: Any) -> Event | None:\n    try:\n        props = feature[\"properties\"]\n        mag = props[\"mag\"]\n        if mag is None:\n            return None\n        lon, lat, depth = feature[\"geometry\"][\"coordinates\"][:3]\n        return Event(\n            id=feature[\"id\"],\n            mag=float(mag),\n            place=props.get(\"place\"),\n            time_ms=int(props[\"time\"]),\n            tsunami=int(props.get(\"tsunami\") or 0),\n            lon=float(lon),\n            lat=float(lat),\n            depth_km=float(depth),\n        )\n    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"malformed feature: {exc!r}\") from Failures surface only as\n`OperationalError`; nothing is written to standard output.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Event:\n    \"\"\"One earthquake, reduced to the fields the reports need.\"\"\"\n\n    id: str\n    mag: float\n    place: str | None\n    time_ms: int\n    tsunami: int\n    lon: float\n    lat: float\n    depth_km: float\n\n\ndef read_feed(path: str | Path) -> list[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return the `features` array of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection file, unchanged.\n\n    Raises `OperationalError` when the file cannot be read, is not JSON, or is not a FeatureCollection\n    object whose `features` value is an array.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}\") from exc\n    try:\n        document = json.loads(text)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not valid JSON\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get(\"type\") != \"FeatureCollection\":\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not a GeoJSON FeatureCollection\")\n    features = document.get(\"features\")\n    if not isinstance(features, list):\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} has no features array\")\n    return features\n\n\ndef extract_events(features: list[Any]) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Turn feed features into `Event` records in feed order, dropping events whose magnitude is null.\"\"\"\n    return [event for event in (_event(feature) for feature in features) if event is not None]\n\n\ndef filter_events(events: list[Event], min_mag: float | None) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Keep events with `mag >= min_mag`, in order. `None` keeps every event.\"\"\"\n    if min_mag is None:\n        return list(events)\n    return [event for event in events if event.mag >= min_mag]\n\n\ndef _event(feature: Any) -> Event | None:\n    try:\n        props = feature[\"properties\"]\n        mag = props[\"mag\"]\n        if mag is None:\n            return None\n        lon, lat, depth = feature[\"geometry\"][\"coordinates\"][:3]\n        return Event(\n            id=feature[\"id\"],\n            mag=float(mag),\n            place=props.get(\"place\"),\n            time_ms=int(props[\"time\"]),\n            tsunami=int(props.get(\"tsunami\") or 0),\n            lon=float(lon),\n            lat=float(lat),\n            depth_km=float(depth),\n        )\n    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"malformed feature: {exc!r}\") from exc\n"}}}

cli.errors import OperationalError\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Event:\n    \"\"\"One earthquake, reduced to the fields the reports need.\"\"\"\n\n    id: str\n    mag: float\n    place: str | None\n    time_ms: int\n    tsunami: int\n    lon: float\n    lat: float\n    depth_km: float\n\n\ndef read_feed(path: str | Path) -> list[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return the `features` array of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection file, unchanged.\n\n    Raises `OperationalError` when the file cannot be read, is not JSON, or is not a FeatureCollection\n    object whose `features` value is an array.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = Path(path).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror or exc}\") from exc\n    try:\n        document = json.loads(text)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not valid JSON\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get(\"type\") != \"FeatureCollection\":\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} is not a GeoJSON FeatureCollection\")\n    features = document.get(\"features\")\n    if not isinstance(features, list):\n        raise OperationalError(f\"{path} has no features array\")\n    return features\n\n\ndef extract_events(features: list[Any]) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Turn feed features into `Event` records in feed order, dropping events whose magnitude is null.\"\"\"\n    return [event for event in (_event(feature) for feature in features) if event is not None]\n\n\ndef filter_events(events: list[Event], min_mag: float | None) -> list[Event]:\n    \"\"\"Keep events with `mag >= min_mag`, in order. `None` keeps every event.\"\"\"\n    if min_mag is None:\n        return list(events)\n    return [event for event in events if event.mag >= min_mag]\n\n\ndef _event(feature: Any) -> Event | None:\n    try:\n        props = feature[\"properties\"]\n        mag = props[\"mag\"]\n        if mag is None:\n            return None\n        lon, lat, depth = feature[\"geometry\"][\"coordinates\"][:3]\n        return Event(\n            id=feature[\"id\"],\n            mag=float(mag),\n            place=props.get(\"place\"),\n            time_ms=int(props[\"time\"]),\n            tsunami=int(props.get(\"tsunami\") or 0),\n            lon=float(lon),\n            lat=float(lat),\n            depth_km=float(depth),\n        )\n    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:\n        raise import datetime, timedelta, timezone\nfrom decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal\nfrom typing import Any, TextIO\n\n_EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n_ISO_UTC = \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\"\n_ONE_PLACE = Decimal(\"0.1\")\n_TWO_PLACES = Decimal(\"0.01\")\n\n\ndef format_time(ms: int | float) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return epoch milliseconds as UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, truncated to whole seconds.\"\"\"\n    seconds = math.floor(ms) // 1000\n    return (_EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=seconds)).strftime(_ISO_UTC)\n\n\ndef format_mag(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a magnitude with exactly one decimal place, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _ONE_PLACE)\n\n\ndef format_mean(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a mean magnitude with two decimal places, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _TWO_PLACES)\n\n\ndef format_decimal(x: Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a depth or distance with one decimal place, rounded half up.\"\"\"\n    return _quantize(x, _ONE_PLACE)\n\n\ndef render_csv(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as CSV text with `\\\\n` line endings; fields with commas or quotes are quoted.\"\"\"\n    buffer = io.StringIO()\n    csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator=\"\\n\").writerows(rows)\n    return buffer.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write_csv(rows: list[list[str]], stream: TextIO | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write `render_csv(rows)` to `stream`, or to standard output as UTF-8 when `stream` is None.\"\"\"\n    text = render_csv(rows)\n    if stream is not None:\n        stream.write(text)\n        return\n    out = sys.stdout\n    binary = getattr(out, \"buffer\", None)\n    if binary is not None:\n        out.flush()\n        binary.write(text.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        binary.flush()\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN5NkeoQEAEhwdbTz3XV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01YGzju7VUMY3Hfnz6W9aHdp","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Quakes/runs/20261025.010423/build/Quakes/cli/__init__.py","content":"\"\"\"Command-line entry point for quakes.\n\n`main` parses the invocation, runs the registered handler, and returns an exit code. It never calls\n`sys.exit`; the `quakes` launcher is the only caller that turns the return value into a process exit.\nA failing command writes nothing to standard output and exactly one line to standard error.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli.errors import QuakesError, UsageError\nfrom cli.formatting import write_stdout\nfrom cli.options import Parsed, parse_args\n\n# Command name -> handler. A handler takes the parsed arguments and returns the full standard-output\n# text; `main` writes that text only after the handler succeeds.\nCOMMANDS: dict[str, Callable[[Parsed], str]] = {}\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run one invocation and return its exit code: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage error.\"\"\"\n    if argv is None:\n        argv = sys.argv[1:]\n    try:\n        parsed = parse_args(argv)\n        handler = COMMANDS.get(parsed.command)\n        if handler is None:\n            raise UsageError(f\"command not available: {parsed.command!r}\")\n        text = handler(parsed)\n    except QuakesError as exc:\n        message = \" \".join(str(exc).split()) or type(exc).__name__\n        print(f\"error: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    write_stdout(text)\n    return 0\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1565,"cache_read_input_tokens":68096,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1565},"output_tokens":16,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d7172c8e-840f-4cd0-9aa0-a0e3de7b7013","uuid":"c22c6686-0f77-4561-a9d6-5a4e8090ec4c","timestamp":"2026-10-25T01:19:47.339Z","request_id":"req_011CgN5NkMCc5DrchPni9GDk","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01YGzju7VUMY3Hfnz6W9aHdp":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Quakes/runs/20261025.010423/build/Quakes/cli/__init__.py","content":"\"\"\"Command-line entry point for quakes.\n\n`main` parses the invocation, runs the registered handler, and returns an exit code. It never calls\n`sys.exit`; the `quakes` launcher is the only caller that turns the return value into a process exit.\nA failing command writes nothing to standard output and exactly one line to standard error.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli.errors import QuakesError, UsageError\nfrom cli.formatting import write_stdout\nfrom cli.options import Parsed, parse_args\n\n# Command name -> handler. A handler takes the parsed arguments and returns the full standard-output\n# text; `main` writes that text only after the handler succeeds.\nCOMMANDS: dict[str, Callable[[Parsed], str]] = {}\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run one invocation and return its exit code: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage error.\"\"\"\n    if argv is None:\n        argv = sys.argv[1:]\n    try:\n        parsed = parse_args(argv)\n        handler = COMMANDS.get(parsed.command)\n        if handler is None:\n            raise UsageError(f\"command not available: {parsed.command!r}\")\n        text = handler(parsed)\n    except QuakesError as exc:\n        message = \" \".join(str(exc).split()) or type(exc).__name__\n        print(f\"error: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    write_stdout(text)\n    return 0\n"}}}

Typed as Any until the options\n# story defines `Parsed`.\nCOMMANDS: dict[str, Callable[[Any], str]] = {}\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run one invocation and return its exit code: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage error.\"\"\"\n    if argv is None:\n        argv = sys.argv[1:]\n    try:\n        command = argv[0] if argv else \"\"\n        if command not in COMMANDS:\n            raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {command!r}\" if command else \"missing command\")\n        # Registered commands are dispatched by the story that adds argument parsing.\n        return 0\n    except UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    except OperationalError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n","userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01YGzju7VUMY3Hfnz6W9aHdp","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

test_main_returns_an_integer_for_an_empty_argv():\n    assert isinstance(main([]), int)\n\n\ndef test_main_returns_usage_exit_code_when_no_command_is_given():\n    assert main([]) == 2\n\n\ndef test_main_returns_usage_exit_code_for_an_unknown_command():\n    assert main([\"no-such-command-xyz\"]) == 2\n\n\ndef test_main_reads_sys_argv_when_argv_is_none(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, \"argv\", [\"quakes\", \"no-such-command-xyz\"])\n    assert main() == 2\n\n\ndef test_main_returns_zero_for_a_registered_command(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"demo\", lambda parsed: \"\")\n    assert main([\"demo\"]) == 0\n\n\ndef test_command_registry_is_a_dict():\n    assert isinstance(cli.COMMANDS, dict)\n\n\ndef test_usage_error_maps_to_exit_code_two():\n    assert UsageError.exit_code == 2\n    assert issubclass(UsageError, Exception)\n\n\ndef test_operational_error_maps_to_exit_code_one():\n    assert OperationalError.exit_code == 1\n    assert issubclass(OperationalError, Exception)\n\n\ndef test_cli_runner_returns_code_stdout_and_stderr_as_text():\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"no-such-command-xyz\")\n    assert isinstance(code, int)\n    assert isinstance(out, str)\n    assert isinstance(err, str)\n\n\ndef test_cli_runner_agrees_with_main_on_exit_code():\n    args = [\"no-such-command-xyz\"]\n    code, _, _ = cli_runner(*args)\n    assert code == main(list(args))\n\n\ndef test_cli_runner_leaves_stdout_empty_on_usage_error():\n    _, out, _ = cli_runner(\"no-such-command-xyz\")\n    assert out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_cli_runner_writes_a_single_diagnostic_line_on_usage_error():\n    _, _, err = cli_runner(\"no-such-command-xyz\")\n    assert \"feed.geojson\"]\n\n\n# ── Declared acceptance assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_options_valid_summary():\n    parsed = parse_args([\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"5.5\", PATH])\n    assert parsed.command == \"summary\"\n    assert parsed.min_mag == 5.5\n    assert parsed.file == PATH\n\n\ndef test_options_defaults():\n    top = parse_args([\"top\", PATH])\n    assert top.n == 10\n    assert top.min_mag is None\n    fetch = parse_args([\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", PATH])\n    assert fetch.min_mag == 2.5\n\n\ndef test_options_any_order():\n    a = parse_args([\"top\", \"--n\", \"3\", \"--min-mag\", \"5.1\", PATH])\n    b = parse_args([\"top\", \"--min-mag\", \"5.1\", \"--n\", \"3\", PATH])\n    assert a.n == b.n == 3\n    assert a.min_mag == b.min_mag == 5.1\n    assert a.file == b.file == PATH\n\n\ndef test_options_near_valid():\n    parsed = parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", \"90\", \"--lon\", \"-180\", \"--radius\", \"0.5\", PATH])\n    assert parsed.lat == 90.0\n    assert parsed.lon == -180.0\n    assert parsed.radius == 0.5\n    negative = parse_args([\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"-1\", PATH])\n    assert negative.min_mag == -1.0\n\n\ndef test_options_fetch_valid():\n    parsed = parse_args(\n        [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--out\", \"feed.geojson\"]\n    )\n    assert parsed.command == \"fetch\"\n    assert parsed.start == \"2025-01-01\"\n    assert parsed.end == \"2025-01-08\"\n    assert parsed.out == \"feed.geojson\"\n    assert parsed.min_mag == 5.0\n\n\ndef test_options_usage_errors():\n    f = PATH\n    bad = [\n        [],\n        [\"frobnicate\", f],\n        [\"near\", \"--lat\", \"27.72\", \"--lon\", \"85.32\", f],\n        [\"near\", \"--lat\", \"95\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"10\", f],\n        [\"near\", \"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"181\", \"--radius\", \"10\", f],\n        [\"near\", \"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"0\", f],\n        [\"top\", \"--n\", \"0\", f],\n        [\"top\", \"--n\", \"2.5\", f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"big\", f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"5.\", f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \".5\", f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", f],\n        [\"summary\"],\n        [\"summary\", f, f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", f],\n        [\"summary\", \"--min-mag\", \"5\", \"--min-mag\", \"6\", f],\n        [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\"],\n        [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--out\", f],\n        [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"2025-01-01\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", f, f],\n        [\"fetch\", \"--start\", \"yesterday\", \"--end\", \"2025-01-08\", \"--out\", f],\n    ]\n    for argv in bad:\n        with pytest.raises(UsageError):\n            parse_args(list(argv))\n\n\ndef test_options_exit_two():\n    code_unknown, out_unknown, _ = cli_runner(\"frobnicate\", PATH)\n    code_none, out_none, _ = cli_runner()\n    assert code_unknown == 2\n    assert code_none == 2\n    assert out_unknown == \"\"\n    assert out_none == \"\"\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: every command, option, boundary, and error path ─────────────────────\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"command\", [\"summary\", \"top\", \"daily\", \"regions\"])\ndef test_report_commands_parse_their_file_argument(command):\n    parsed = parse_args([command, PATH])\n    assert parsed.command == command\n    assert parsed.file == PATH\n    assert parsed.min_mag is None\n\n\ndef test_report_commands_do_not_touch_the_file_system(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n    missing = tmp_path / \"no-such-file.geojson\"\n    assert parse_args([\"summary\", str(missing)]).file == str(missing)\n\n\ndef test_near_parses_all_required_options_with_min_mag():\n    parsed = parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", \"27.72\", \"--lon\", \"85.32\", \"--radius\", \"800\", \"--min-mag\", \"5.3\", PATH])\n    assert (parsed.lat, parsed.lon, parsed.radius, parsed.min_mag) == (27.72, 85.32, 800.0, 5.3)\n    assert parsed.file == PATH\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"lat\", [\"-90\", \"90\", \"0\", \"-45.5\"])\ndef test_near_latitude_accepts_the_full_range(lat):\n    assert parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", lat, \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"1\", PATH]).lat == parse_args([\"near\", \"--lat\", lat, \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"1\", PATH])\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"lon\", [\"-180\", \"180\", \"0\"])\ndef result.returncode == main([\"frobnicate\"]) == 2","originalFile":"\"\"\"Exit-code story: UsageError exits 2, OperationalError exits 1, success exits 0, all via `main`.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport cli\nfrom cli import main\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, UsageError\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nPATH = \"quakes-file.geojson\"\n\n\ndef _failing(parsed):\n    raise OperationalError(\"cannot read the file\")\n\n\n# ── Declared acceptance assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_exit_usage_code():\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"frobnicate\", PATH)\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_exit_operational_code(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"summary\", _failing)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"summary\", PATH)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_exit_success_code(monkeypatch):\n    text = \"header\\nrow\\n\"\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"daily\", lambda parsed: text)\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"daily\", PATH)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out == text\n\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"daily\", lambda parsed: \"\")\n    empty_code, empty_out, _ = cli_runner(\"daily\", PATH)\n    assert empty_code == 0\n    assert empty_out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_exit_error_classes():\n    assert issubclass(UsageError, Exception)\n    assert issubclass(OperationalError, Exception)\n    assert not issubclass(UsageError, OperationalError)\n    assert not issubclass(OperationalError, UsageError)\n\n\ndef test_exit_launcher_status():\n    result = subprocess.run([str(ROOT / \"quakes\"), \"frobnicate\", PATH], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)\n    assert result.returncode == 2\n    assert result.stdout == \"\"\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: failure silence, one diagnostic line, and unmapped exceptions ───────\n\n\ndef test_usage_exit_code_is_two_and_operational_is_one():\n    assert UsageError.exit_code == 2\n    assert OperationalError.exit_code == 1\n\n\ndef test_operational_failure_prints_exactly_one_stderr_line_without_stdout(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"summary\", _failing)\n    code = main([\"summary\", PATH])\n    captured = capsys.readouterr()\n    assert code == 1\n    assert captured.out == \"\"\n    assert captured.err == \"error: cannot read the file\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_multiline_message_is_squeezed_onto_one_stderr_line(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    def multi(parsed):\n        raise OperationalError(\"first line\\nsecond line\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"summary\", multi)\n    code = main([\"summary\", PATH])\n    captured = capsys.readouterr()\n    assert code == 1\n    assert captured.out == \"\"\n    assert len(captured.err.splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_usage_failure_writes_nothing_to_stdout(capsys):\n    assert main([\"summary\", \"--n\", \"3\", PATH]) == 2\n    captured = capsys.readouterr()\n    assert captured.out == \"\"\n    assert len(captured.err.splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_handler_output_is_written_only_on_success(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"summary\", lambda parsed: \"events\\n0\\n\")\n    assert main([\"summary\", PATH]) == 0\n    assert capsys.readouterr().out == \"events\\n0\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_failing_handler_writes_no_partial_output(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    def partial(parsed):\n        raise OperationalError(\"boom\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"top\", partial)\n    assert main([\"top\", PATH]) == 1\n    assert capsys.readouterr().out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_unexpected_exception_is_not_mapped_to_an_exit_code(monkeypatch):\n    def broken(parsed):\n        raise RuntimeError(\"bug\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, \"summary\", broken)\n    try:\n        main([\"summary\", PATH])\n    except RuntimeError as exc:\n        assert str(exc) == \"bug\"\n    else:\n        raise AssertionError(\"an unexpected exception must assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert len(err.splitlines()) == 1\n\n\ndef test_exit_success_code(monkeypatch):\n    text = \"header\\nrow\\n\"\n    monkeypatch.setitem(cli.COMMANDS, depth\n\n\ndef test_extract_null_mag_excluded():\n    features = [_feature(\"a\", 5.0), _feature(\"b\", None), _feature(\"c\", 0), _feature(\"d\", 6.1), _feature(\"e\", None)]\n    events = extract_events(features)\n    kept_ids = [f[\"id\"] for f in features if f[\"properties\"][\"mag\"] is not None]\n    assert [e.id for e in events] == kept_ids\n    assert len(events) == assert events[0].place is None\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: absent optional fields, field selection, and malformed input ────────\n\n\ndef test_missing_tsunami_is_read_as_zero():\n    feature = [\"zero\"]\n    assert events[0].mag == 0.0\n\n\ndef test_depth_is_the_third_coordinate_and_extra_coordinates_are_ignored():\n    feature = _feature(\"d\", 5.0)\n isinstance(event.time_ms, int)\n    assert isinstance(event.tsunami, int)\n    assert isinstance(event.lon, float)\n    assert isinstance(event.depth_km, float)\n\n\ndef test_event_is_immutable():\n    event = extract_events([_feature(\"i\", 5.0)])[0]\n    assert isinstance(event, Event)\n    with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):\n        event.mag = 9.0\n\n\ndef test_feed_order_is_preserved_for_many_features():\n    features = [_feature(f\"e{i}\", 5.0 + i / 10) for i in range(25)]\n    assert [e.id for e in extract_events(features)] == [f\"e{i}\" for i in test_extraction_does_not_mutate_the_features():\n    features = [_feature(\"m\", 5.0)]\n    snapshot = [dict(f, properties=dict(f[\"properties\"])) for f in features]\n    extract_events(features)\n test_testsuite_propagates_failure(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_fails.py\", \"def test_always_fails():\\n    assert False\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_passes_when_tests_pass(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_passes.py\", \"def test_always_passes():\\n    assert True\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) == 0\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: working directory, environment, and the script's own contract ───────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_runs_from_another_directory_with_the_same_status(tmp_path):\n    app = tmp_path / \"app\"\n    app.mkdir()\n    for name in (\"cli\", \"bin\", \"tests\"):\n        shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, app / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(\"__pycache__\", \".pytest_cache\"))\n    (app / \"tests\" / THIS_FILE).unlink()\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"conftest.py\", app / \"conftest.py\")\n test_testsuite_fails_when_a_test_errors_at_import(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_broken_import.py\", \"import no_such_module_quakes\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_runs_only_the_suite_and_is_executable_by_sh():\n    result = subprocess.run([\"sh\", \"-n\", str(SCRIPT)], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert The runner is\nexercised on temporary application roots that hold only the tests each case needs.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nSCRIPT = ROOT / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\"\nTHIS_FILE = Path(__file__).name\n\n\ndef _env_with_pytest() -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {**os.environ, \"PATH\": os.path.dirname(sys.executable) + os.pathsep + os.environ.get(\"PATH\", \"\")}\n\n\ndef _make_root(root: Path, test_name: str, test_body: str) -> Path:\n    (root / \"bin\").mkdir()\n    (root / \"tests\").mkdir()\n    shutil.copy(SCRIPT, root / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\")\n    (root / \"tests\" / test_name).write_text(test_body, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return root\n\n\ndef _run_runner(root: Path, cwd: Path) -> int:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"sh\", str(root / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\")], capture_output=True, text=True, env=_env_with_pytest(), cwd=cwd\n    )\n    return result.returncode\n\n\n# ── Declared acceptance assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_exists():\n    assert SCRIPT.is_file()\n    first_line = SCRIPT.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()[0]\n    assert first_line.startswith(\"#!\")\n    assert first_line.rstrip().endswith(\"sh\")\n    assert \"bash\" not in first_line\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_propagates_failure(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_fails.py\", \"def test_always_fails():\\n    assert False\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_passes_when_tests_pass(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_passes.py\", \"def test_always_passes():\\n    assert True\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) == 0\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: working directory, environment, and the script's own contract ───────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_runs_from_another_directory_with_the_same_status(tmp_path):\n    app = tmp_path / \"app\"\n    app.mkdir()\n    for name in (\"cli\", \"bin\", \"tests\"):\n        shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, app / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(\"__pycache__\", \".pytest_cache\"))\n    (app / \"tests\" / THIS_FILE).unlink()\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"conftest.py\", app / \"conftest.py\")\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"pyproject.toml\", app / \"pyproject.toml\")\n\n    elsewhere = tmp_path / \"elsewhere\"\n    elsewhere.mkdir()\n    assert _run_runner(app, elsewhere) == 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_fails_when_a_test_errors_at_import(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_broken_import.py\", \"import no_such_module_quakes\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_runs_only_the_suite_and_is_executable_by_sh():\n    result = subprocess.run([\"sh\", \"-n\", str(SCRIPT)], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nSCRIPT = ROOT / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\"\nTHIS_FILE = Path(__file__).name\n\n\ndef _env_with_pytest() -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {**os.environ, \"PATH\": os.path.dirname(sys.executable) + os.pathsep + os.environ.get(\"PATH\", \"\")}\n\n\ndef _make_root(root: Path, test_name: str, test_body: str) -> Path:\n    (root / \"bin\").mkdir()\n    (root / Path, cwd: Path) -> int:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"sh\", str(root / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\")], capture_output=True, text=True, env=_env_with_pytest(), cwd=cwd\n    )\n    return result.returncode\n\n\n# ── Declared acceptance assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_exists():\n    assert SCRIPT.is_file()\n    first_line test_testsuite_propagates_failure(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_fails.py\", \"def test_always_fails():\\n    assert False\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_passes_when_tests_pass(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_passes.py\", \"def test_always_passes():\\n    assert True\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) == 0\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: working directory, environment, and the script's own contract ───────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_runs_from_another_directory_with_the_same_status(tmp_path):\n    app = tmp_path / \"app\"\n    app.mkdir()\n    for name in (\"cli\", \"bin\", \"tests\"):\n        shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, app / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(\"__pycache__\", \".pytest_cache\"))\n    (app / \"tests\" / THIS_FILE).unlink()\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"conftest.py\", app / \"conftest.py\")\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"pyproject.toml\", app / \"pyproject.toml\")\n\n    elsewhere = tmp_path / \"elsewhere\"\n    elsewhere.mkdir()\n    assert _run_runner(app, elsewhere) == 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_fails_when_a_test_errors_at_import(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_broken_import.py\", \"import no_such_module_quakes\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_parses_under_sh():\n    result = subprocess.run([\"sh\", \"-n\", str(SCRIPT)], capture_output=True, text=True)\n    assert result.returncode == Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nSCRIPT = ROOT / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\"\nTHIS_FILE = Path(__file__).name\n\n\ndef _env_with_pytest() -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {**os.environ, \"PATH\": os.path.dirname(sys.executable) + os.pathsep + os.environ.get(\"PATH\", \"\")}\n\n\ndef _make_root(root: Path, test_name: str, test_body: str) -> Path:\n    (root / \"bin\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    (root / \"tests\").mkdir()\n    shutil.copy(SCRIPT, root / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\")\n    (root / \"tests\" / test_name).write_text(test_body, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return root\n\n\ndef _run_runner(root: Path, cwd: Path) -> int:\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [\"sh\", str(root / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\")], capture_output=True, text=True, env=_env_with_pytest(), cwd=cwd\n    )\n    return result.returncode\n\n\n# ── Declared acceptance assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_script_exists():\n    assert SCRIPT.is_file()\n    first_line = SCRIPT.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()[0]\n    assert first_line.startswith(\"#!\")\n    assert first_line.rstrip().endswith(\"sh\")\n    assert \"bash\" not in first_line\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_propagates_failure(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_fails.py\", \"def test_always_fails():\\n    assert False\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) != 0\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_passes_when_tests_pass(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_always_passes.py\", \"def test_always_passes():\\n    assert True\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root, root) == 0\n\n\n# ── Finer coverage: working directory, environment, and the script's own contract ───────\n\n\ndef test_testsuite_runs_from_another_directory_with_the_same_status(tmp_path):\n    app = tmp_path / \"app\"\n    app.mkdir()\n    for name in (\"cli\", \"bin\", \"tests\"):\n        shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, app / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(\"__pycache__\", \".pytest_cache\"))\n    (app / \"tests\" / THIS_FILE).unlink()\n    shutil.copy(ROOT / \"conftest.py\", app / \"conftest.py\")\n test_testsuite_fails_when_a_test_errors_at_import(tmp_path):\n    root = _make_root(tmp_path / \"app\", \"test_broken_import.py\", \"import no_such_module_quakes\\n\")\n    assert _run_runner(root,
